name: The Coherence Equation™
variables: C=Coherence; A=Alignment; I=Integrity; E=Expressed Energy; D=Distortion
axiom: Coherence increases when alignment, integrity, and expressed energy converge, and degrades as distortion accumulates.
interpretation: Coherence is not agreement. It is the structural stability produced when intention, architecture, action, and consequence point in the same direction.

name: The Recognition Equation™
variables: R=Recognition; V=Value Created; C=Coherence; I=Integrity; t=Time
axiom: Recognition is delayed coherence observed across time.
interpretation: Recognition is not a demand. It is the cumulative effect of value expressed coherently and consistently until the signal becomes visible.

name: The Trust Equation™
axiom: Trust increases when consistency and provenance reduce uncertainty.
interpretation: Trust is not a mood. In systems architecture, trust becomes observable through repeated reliability, traceability, and the reduction of unresolved ambiguity.

name: The Observability Principle™
axiom: A system becomes more observable when meaningful signal exceeds informational noise.
interpretation: The problem is not always absence of information. Often the problem is excessive noise, poor instrumentation, or unstructured information that blocks interpretation.

name: The Reciprocity Equation™
axiom: Reciprocity is balanced contribution across time, not identical exchange in a single moment.
interpretation: Reciprocity measures whether energy, care, labor, value, and acknowledgment move through a relationship or system without permanent extraction.

name: The Knowledge Conservation Principle™
variables: Kₜ=Total Knowledge; Kₛ=Structured Knowledge; Kₐ=Accessible Knowledge; Kₚ=Preserved Provenance; Kₗ=Lost Context
axiom: Knowledge is not destroyed so much as fragmented, buried, misclassified, or severed from context.
interpretation: The architecture determines whether knowledge compounds or decays into inaccessible fragments.

name: The Complexity Gradient™
variables: Gx=Complexity Gradient; ΔCₓ=Change in System Complexity; ΔS=Change in Structure
axiom: Complexity becomes dangerous when it grows faster than structure.
interpretation: Complex systems do not need to be simplified into false clarity; they need enough structure to make their relationships navigable.

name: The Alignment Function™
axiom: Alignment is measured through longitudinal consistency, not declarations.
interpretation: A system reveals its alignment through repeated decisions under changing conditions.

name: The Signal Hierarchy™
variables: Sₕ=Signal Hierarchy; W=Words; A=Actions; P=Patterns; T=Time
axiom: Words initiate signal; actions amplify it; patterns validate it; time reveals it.
interpretation: SOVRINT™ treats isolated claims as weak evidence and repeated patterns as stronger observables.

name: The Architect's Axiom™
variables: Civilization=Emergent social order; Systems=Architected relationships among values knowledge infrastructure and time
axiom: People build products; architects build systems; systems build civilizations.
interpretation: The highest level of work is not output production, but the construction of architectures that continue producing coherent outputs after the first builder leaves the room.

name: The Distortion Load™
variables: Dₗ=Distortion Load; N=Noise; U=Uncertainty; B=Bias; H=Hidden Incentives
axiom: Distortion accumulates when noise, uncertainty, bias, and hidden incentives remain uncorrected.
interpretation: SOVRINT™ treats distortion as a measurable burden on decision quality, trust, and institutional stability.

name: The Lineage Rule™
variables: Lr=Lineage Reliability; O=Origin; V=Versioning; P=Provenance; C=Continuity
axiom: A system without lineage cannot reliably prove what it is, where it came from, or how it changed.
interpretation: Lineage is the memory architecture of trust.
